ordered_diagnoses: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type
Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type

facts.raw_span: painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis of 1 month's duration
elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy discovered 9 years prior
fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite
asymptomatic 'green-yellow welts' and swelling of the glans penis
swelling became progressively painful and evolved to the size of an 'orange' over 4 days
no improvement with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin
glans penis and corona were grossly edematous
3.7 × 3.3-cm tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar, adherent yellow crust, and granulation tissue
no urethral discharge was present
routine blood test results were within normal limits
dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes, which were CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, within the background of a reactive T-cell infiltrate
clonal IgH gene rearrangement

concepts.why: The presence of a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes with specific immunophenotypic markers (CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+) and a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, along with a large and firm ulcer on the penis, supports this diagnosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type
concepts.why: Although the location is unusual, the specific immunophenotypic markers and clonal IgH gene rearrangement could suggest a variant of this disease, given the aggressive nature of the presentation.

concepts.preferred_label: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type
concepts.why: The presence of a destructive lesion and specific immunophenotypic markers, although not perfectly matching, could suggest this rare and aggressive lymphoma in the differential diagnosis, especially considering the lack of typical NK cell markers in the provided information.
Although less likely given the specific lymphocyte markers, the skin involvement and progression could mimic this disease, especially if considering a transformation or an unusual presentation.
The presence of a clonal IgH gene rearrangement and specific lymphocyte markers could suggest this disease, although the clinical presentation is less typical for MCL.

rationales.F01: The presence of painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis is more typical of lymphoma, particularly diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
rationales.F08: The presence of a tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar, adherent yellow crust, and granulation tissue is highly suggestive of lymphoma.
rationales.F11: The dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes with specific immunophenotypic markers is diagnostic of B-cell lymphoma.
rationales.F12: The clonal IgH gene rearrangement is a specific marker for B-cell lymphoma, making it highly likely.

frontier_selector.runner_up: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type
frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes that are CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, along with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, strongly supports the diagnosis of a B-cell lymphoma. The clinical presentation and the absence of specific markers for other types of lymphoma make Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma the most fitting diagnosis.
